plugins.name: meeting-wiki
plugins.description: Turn meeting transcripts into an evolving, interlinked markdown wiki — people, projects, topics, decisions, and action items kept up to date by Claude.

plugins.name: plugin-creator
plugins.description: Author Claude Code plugin marketplaces — scaffold plugins, enforce authoring rules, validate the catalog (schema + skills.sh discoverability), and bump/release versions.

plugins.name: feature-qa
plugins.description: Generate MANUAL-only QA test plans and execute them to satisfy Jira ticket requirements without breaking existing features; capture evidence and comment test results.

plugins.name: feature-code-review
plugins.description: Unbiased, impact-driven code review of a feature anchored to its Jira ticket — review the diff plus related code across performance, security, responsiveness, error handling, UX, reusable components, and structure; skip per-line nits; post on PASS only after you confirm.

plugins.name: idea-to-ticket
plugins.description: Turn a raw idea into well-formed Jira ticket(s) — interrogate vague input, assess the codebase for collisions, draft caveman-lite title/description/acceptance-criteria, and create in Jira only with explicit human approval; post dev assessment + test plan as a comment.

plugins.name: vibe-coding-essentials
plugins.description: Guardrails for AI-assisted rapid coding — PostToolUse scanners for secrets/security/format/types on every edit, five reusable rulesets (security, clean-code, git, testing, project-setup) loadable per session, plus on-demand secret-scan, security-audit, and refactor-plan skills.

plugins.name: dev-assessment
plugins.description: Turn an existing Jira ticket into an engineering scoping assessment — check ticket info is sufficient (always ask the human when not), scan the whole workspace not just one repo, write a caveman-lite assessment (complexity, affected code & repos, approach, risks, open questions), and post it to Jira only after human approval.

plugins.name: prompt-craft
plugins.description: Diagnose a weak prompt and rewrite it to Anthropic's prompt-engineering best practices — clarity, context/motivation, examples in <example> tags, XML structure, role, tell-what-to-do framing, calibrated thinking/tool/agentic guidance — without over-prompting or redesigning the task; outputs before/after plus what changed and why.
